semantic_slots.objects: Matches: the data are a measure mu on A, kernels R:A→B and F:A×B→B, the fiber comap F_a, the joint measure P (called M by the decoder), and the actual kernel K obtained by taking the product of the deterministic first projection with F.
semantic_slots.domains: Matches: A and B carry arbitrary measurable-space structures; A×B carries the product structure. R(a) and F(a,b) are measures on B. The fiber events are measurable subsets of B, and the joint events are arbitrary measurable subsets of A×B, not only rectangles. Fluxes are ENNReal integrals.
semantic_slots.quantifiers: Matches: A, B, their measurable structures, mu, R and F are generic with the listed instances. The hypothesis is for mu-almost every a, for every measurable pair of fiber events, in that order. The conclusion is for every measurable pair of joint events. No common conull set is inferred from separately exceptional event pairs.
semantic_slots.assumptions: Matches: SFinite mu is a countable sum of finite measures; IsSFiniteKernel R and F are countable sums of finite kernels, not merely pointwise conditions on their output measures. Kernel measurability of F is joint in (a,b); it is not an extra premise. The only balance premise is reversibility of the fiber comap under R(a) almost everywhere. No sigma-finiteness, finite flux, Markovness, nonemptiness or standard Borel structure is required.
semantic_slots.conclusion: Matches: (deterministic Prod.fst ×ₖ F).IsReversible (mu ⊗ₘ R), i.e. equality of the two extended nonnegative fluxes for all measurable joint S,T. The formula K((a,b),T)=F(a,b)(T_a) identifies the actual update; invariance is not a second formal conclusion.
semantic_slots.senses: Matches: reversibility is setwise flux symmetry, including equality of infinite fluxes, not a definition carrying normalization or stationarity. P is a measure–kernel comp-product with possibly varying R(a), not an independent product. The non-Markov use of the second-coordinate update refers to an assigned measure, not necessarily a probability draw.
semantic_slots.constants: Matches: no numerical coefficients, rates or time parameters occur in the theorem. The only unit mass is the Dirac measure at the input's first coordinate in the deterministic factor, which does not normalize F or K. The fiber comap is along the constant-a/identity-b inclusion; ×ₖ and ⊗ₘ have the distinct kernel product and measure–kernel comp-product senses.

For fixed a, b↦(a,b) is measurable, giving S_a and T_a by preimage. The measurable deterministic projection and s-finite kernel product give a kernel K, so its evaluation at measurable T is measurable in (a,b). Kernel.deterministic_prod_apply' gives the section evaluation for any measurable T. Applying the measurable indicator of S gives the jointly measurable integrand needed for comp-product integration.

Measure.lintegral_compProd applies with SFinite mu and IsSFiniteKernel R to the nonnegative indicator integrand. It yields the iterated integral with the inner integral over S_a of F(a,b)(T_a) against R(a). This is legitimate without probability, finiteness of the value, subtraction of infinities or independence of R(a) from a. S-finiteness of F is used in the deterministic product interface, not added as a separate fiber-integrability premise.

On the conull condition where the entire comapped fiber kernel is reversible, use the measurable S_a and T_a for that a; they may depend on a. The inner expressions for (S,T) and (T,S) are therefore equal mu-almost everywhere. Apply lintegral_congr_ae and the same comp-product identity in reverse. There is no uncountable intersection of event-specific null exceptions.

Taking S=A×B identifies (P K)(T) with the integral over T of K(z,A×B) against P; Markov normalization makes this P(T). Without normalization there is no general implication: on singleton measurable A and B take mu and R(a) to be unit Dirac masses and F=0. Then P is unit mass, all stated hypotheses hold, K=0 and both fluxes are zero, but P K is zero and differs from P on the full space. This refutes general implication, not invariance for every non-Markov kernel.

They neither award invariance as a Lean result nor require a particular notation or tactic.

Credit equivalent correct measurability and flux proofs, including an equivalent integration or transport argument that genuinely reaches arbitrary measurable joint events and correctly uses the given a.e. hypothesis. Showing balance only for rectangles, appealing to measure uniqueness without validating its premises, or replacing the full-fiber a.e. statement by an unsupported common-null-set inference does not suffice.
